description: This PIARC report (2022R33EN) collects case studies on climate change, other hazards and the resilience of road networks. It was produced by Technical Committee 1.4 on climate change and resilience of road networks in the 2020 to 2023 cycle, whose two working groups aim to develop uniform methods and guidance. A survey gathered 71 studies from 24 countries on six continents; part 1 gives the collection process, methodological background and statistics and summarises definitions of resilience, and the studies follow. Coverage: road agencies worldwide. Format and access: PDF (5.2 MB) from the PIARC virtual library, whose site asks users to accept cookies and sign in to their personal space to download. Licence and cost: under PIARC terms; the page lists the file for download. Caveats: case studies are self-reported by agencies and vary in depth. It supports climate adaptation, resilience and hazard exposure studies of road networks by pointing to comparable cases. It relates to the PIARC adaptation framework 2023 and the FHWA resilience pilots in the catalogue.
